prompt_text: Train a classifier on the data in this directory (README.md describes it) and report its held-out performance. Python (numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn) is available; create scripts with the Write tool.
answer:
Proteins are shared entities; check overlap and entity-memorization baseline alongside the model.I trained two classifiers on `coexpression_z` and scored them on the test pairs. Held-out AUROC is about 0.65 for logistic regression and about 0.67 for gradient boosting.

| Model | Test AUROC |
|---|---|
| Logistic regression | 0.652 |
| Gradient boosting | 0.672 |

Five-fold cross-validation on the training set gives 0.648 for logistic regression, close to the test score. Positives are about 17% of both sets, so a random classifier scores 0.5.

**Protein overlap:** every test pair has both of its proteins in the training set (100% overlap). A baseline that uses no features can exploit this. It predicts each test pair from how often its two proteins were positive in training, and it scores AUROC 0.82, higher than either model. Some proteins are probably "sticky" in the screen, meaning they interact with many partners. So these test scores measure interpolation within a known set of proteins. They don't show how well the model would predict interactions for new proteins.

I didn't run a split that holds out proteins, so I can't say how much of the 0.65 comes from co-expression alone. If you need generalization to unseen proteins, I can build a split where test proteins never appear in training and re-evaluate.

I also didn't call the audit tools on the MCP server, so the overlap check above is my own, not theirs. The script is `run.py` in the analysis directory.

input.command: cd /tmp/review-xypxwsfl/analysis && head -5 pairs_train.csv pairs_test.csv; ls .devin; wc -l *.csv

cd /tmp/review-xypxwsfl/analysis && cat > run.py <<'E'
import pandas as pd,numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score as A
tr=pd.read_csv('pairs_train.csv');te=pd.read_csv('pairs_test.csv')
print(tr.label.mean(),te.label.mean())
for m in [LogisticRegression(),GradientBoostingClassifier()]:
    m.fit(tr[['coexpression_z']],tr.label);print(type(m).__name__,A(te.label,m.predict_proba(te[['coexpression_z']])[:,1]))
ptr=set(tr.protein_a)|set(tr.protein_b)
print('test rows with both/any protein in train:',te.apply(lambda r:r.protein_a in ptr and r.protein_b in ptr,axis=1).mean(),te.apply(lambda r:r.protein_a in ptr or r.protein_b in ptr,axis=1).mean())
# per-protein label rate baseline
s={};c={}
for _,r in tr.iterrows():
    for p in(r.protein_a,r.protein_b):s[p]=s.get(p,0)+r.label;c[p]=c.get(p,0)+1
g=tr.label.mean()
f=lambda p:(s.get(p,0)+g*2)/(c.get(p,0)+2)
sc=te.apply(lambda r:(f(r.protein_a)+f(r.protein_b))/2,axis=1)
print('entity baseline AUROC',A(te.label,sc))
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
print('cv coexp',cross_val_score(LogisticRegression(),tr[['coexpression_z']],tr.label,scoring='roc_auc').mean())
E
python run.py
